"'''Blaze of Glory'''" is the debut solo single of American singer-songwriter [[Jon Bon Jovi]]. It was released in July 1990 by [[Mercury Records]] as the lead single from his first solo album, ''[[Blaze of Glory (Jon Bon Jovi album)|Blaze of Glory]]'' (1990). The song was written by Bon Jovi and co-produced by him with [[Danny Kortchmar]]. It reached {{abbr|No.|Number}} 1 on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and [[Album Rock Tracks]] charts in 1990, becoming his only chart-topper away from his band [[Bon Jovi]]. "Blaze of Glory" also topped the [[ARIA Charts|Australian]], [[RPM (magazine)|Canadian]], and [[Recorded Music NZ|New Zealand]] singles charts and reached No. 13 on the [[UK Singles Chart]].

"Blaze of Glory" is the debut solo single of American singer-songwriter Jon Bon Jovi. It was released in July 1990 by Mercury Records as the lead single from his first solo album, Blaze of Glory (1990). The song was written by Bon Jovi and co-produced by him with Danny Kortchmar. It reached {{abbr|No.|Number}} 1 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and Album Rock Tracks charts in 1990, becoming his only chart-topper away from his band Bon Jovi. "Blaze of Glory" also topped the Australian, Canadian, and New Zealand singles charts and reached No. 13 on the UK Singles Chart.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
The [[power ballad]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/uk/go/44642|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180927180222/http://www.denofgeek.com/uk/go/44642|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 27, 2018|title=24 of the Biggest and Best Movie Power Ballads|website=Denofgeek.com|access-date=March 3, 2022}}</ref> was allegedly recorded by Jon Bon Jovi because [[Emilio Estevez]] requested Bon Jovi's song "[[Wanted Dead or Alive (Bon Jovi song)|Wanted Dead or Alive]]" for the soundtrack to ''[[Young Guns II]]'', but Jon did not think the lyrics—about the band constantly touring—fit the theme of the Western movie. However, the request inspired him to write "Blaze of Glory" with lyrics more topical to the film.

In 1990, guitarist [[Aldo Nova]] wrote the main guitar riff used in "Blaze of Glory".<ref name="LarkinHR">{{cite book|title=[[Encyclopedia of Popular Music|The Virgin Encyclopedia of Heavy Rock]]|editor=[[Colin Larkin (writer)|Colin Larkin]]|publisher=[[Virgin Books]]|date=1999|edition=First|isbn=0-7535-0257-7|page=326}}</ref>  In 1991, to return the favor, Jon Bon Jovi worked with Nova to release ''[[Blood on the Bricks (Aldo Nova album)|Blood on the Bricks]]'' on Bon Jovi's label Jambco Records.<ref name="LarkinHR" />

The song features a music video and remains a crowd favorite with Bon Jovi fans, despite the fact that the song was not released as one of the band's singles, and only by Jon. The song was included on both Bon Jovi greatest hits compilations: 1994's ''[[Cross Road (album)|Cross Road]]'' and 2008's ''[[Greatest Hits (Bon Jovi album)|Greatest Hits]]''. The track is notable for the performance of [[Jeff Beck]] on guitar. The music video was filmed at [[The Rectory (Utah)|The Rectory]] near [[Moab, Utah]].
sections.text:
The power ballad was allegedly recorded by Jon Bon Jovi because Emilio Estevez requested Bon Jovi's song "Wanted Dead or Alive" for the soundtrack to Young Guns II, but Jon did not think the lyrics—about the band constantly touring—fit the theme of the Western movie. However, the request inspired him to write "Blaze of Glory" with lyrics more topical to the film.

In 1990, guitarist Aldo Nova wrote the main guitar riff used in "Blaze of Glory".  In 1991, to return the favor, Jon Bon Jovi worked with Nova to release Blood on the Bricks on Bon Jovi's label Jambco Records.

The song features a music video and remains a crowd favorite with Bon Jovi fans, despite the fact that the song was not released as one of the band's singles, and only by Jon. The song was included on both Bon Jovi greatest hits compilations: 1994's Cross Road and 2008's Greatest Hits. The track is notable for the performance of Jeff Beck on guitar. The music video was filmed at The Rectory near Moab, Utah.
